subject: lacewing larva
title: This Larva Wears Its Victims' Wool So Their Ant Guards Ignore It

scenes.text: This tiny larva walks into a herd guarded by ants, and eats the herd.
The herd is woolly alder aphids, covered in white wax fluff. Ants guard them for their sweet honeydew.
Any normal predator gets attacked. This green lacewing larva plucks the wax right off its prey.
It piles the fluff on its own back in under twenty minutes, and now it passes as an aphid.
Scientists stripped the coat off. The ants grabbed the larvae and carried them away.
With the coat on, it eats in peace. A wolf in sheep's clothing, for real.

description:
Larvae of the green lacewing Chrysopa slossonae live among woolly alder aphids, which are guarded by ants. The larva plucks the aphids' waxy wool and loads it onto its own back, and the ants leave it alone while it eats the aphids.
In experiments (Eisner et al., Science, 1978), larvae stripped of their coat were seized by ants and removed. Coating takes under 20 minutes on average.
What's the sneakiest animal disguise you know?
thumbnail_text: WEARS ITS PREY. FOOLS THE ANTS
first_comment: The larva treats putting its disguise back on as about as urgent as eating. Which animal trick fools you every time?
